result.markdown: --- title: "Session 4 — Cox Proportional Hazards Regression" subtitle: "Hazard ratios · multiple predictors · scaling · events per variable · predicted curves · Lab 4" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 2–3: describe and compare curves - Today: **regression for survival**: effect sizes, adjustment for several variables - By the end you can: - fit a **Cox model** and interpret a **hazard ratio** and its CI - fit and report a **multivariable** model - **scale** continuous variables and check **events per variable** - draw a **predicted survival curve** for a patient profile ::: # Topic 1 — The hazard ratio {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## The model ::: {.eq} h(t | x) = h~0~(t) × exp(β~1~x~1~ + β~2~x~2~ + …) ::: ::: {.incremental} - **h~0~(t)** is an unspecified **baseline hazard**: the shape over time is left free - **exp(β)** is the **hazard ratio**: the **multiplicative** change in the hazard for a one-unit increase in x, **at any time** - **Proportional hazards:** that ratio is **constant over time** (checked in Session 5) - Like logistic regression it uses **exp(coefficient)**, but it models **rates over time** ::: ## One predictor ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cox1 <- coxph(Surv(time_months, status) ~ hiv, data = tb) exp(cbind(HR = coef(cox1), confint(cox1))) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` HR 2.5 % 97.5 % hivPositive 1.8 1.1 2.95 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **HR = 1.8** (95% CI 1.1–2.9): at any time, the **hazard of death is about 80% higher** in HIV-positive patients. It is a **rate ratio, not a risk ratio**; and unlike the log-rank test it has a **size and a CI**. ::: # Topic 2 — Adjusted model {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Several predictors at once ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cox_full <- coxph(Surv(time_months, status) ~ age + sex + hiv + diabetes + smoker + bmi + mdr_tb + treatment, data = tb) round(exp(cbind(HR = coef(cox_full), confint(cox_full))), 2) # tbl_regression(cox_full, exponentiate = TRUE) formats this for a paper ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` HR 2.5 % 97.5 % age 1.01 1.00 1.03 sexMale 1.08 0.72 1.64 hivPositive 1.96 1.18 3.25 diabetesYes 1.37 0.69 2.75 smokerYes 1.10 0.73 1.66 bmi 0.92 0.86 0.98 mdr_tbYes 2.11 1.25 3.58 treatmentDOT 0.57 0.39 0.83 ``` ::: ::: ## Reading the adjusted hazard ratios ::: {.incremental} - Each HR is **adjusted for the others**: "holding age, sex, … fixed" - **MDR-TB** about doubles the hazard; **DOT** about halves it (reference: self-administered); sex shows no effect - The **CI** shows the precision: a CI that includes **1** means no clear association ::: ## Reading continuous predictors ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cox_age10 <- coxph(Surv(time_months, status) ~ I(age / 10) + hiv + mdr_tb + treatment, data = tb) round(exp(cbind(HR = coef(cox_age10), confint(cox_age10))), 2)[1, ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` HR 2.5 % 97.5 % 1.16 1.01 1.33 ``` ::: ::: The HR for age is for **one year** unless you rescale: **per 10 years** is a more readable unit (HR^10). For BMI, use a clinically sensible step (per 5 kg/m²). ## Events per variable ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(events = sum(tb$status), coefficients = length(coef(cox_full)), events_per_coefficient = round(sum(tb$status) / length(coef(cox_full)), 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` events coefficients events_per_coefficient 113.0 8.0 14.1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} The information in a Cox model is the **number of events**, not the number of patients. As a rule of thumb, aim for **about 10 or more events per coefficient**; with fewer, estimates are unstable and the model overfits. Choose predictors **from theory** first (Session 6 of the regression workshop). ::: # Topic 3 — Using the model {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Predicted survival for a patient profile ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} nd <- tibble(age = 40, sex = "Male", hiv = c("Negative", "Positive"), diabetes = "No", smoker = "No", bmi = 20, mdr_tb = "No", treatment = "DOT") |> mutate(across(c(sex, hiv, diabetes, smoker, mdr_tb, treatment), \(v) factor(v, levels = levels(tb[[cur_column()]])))) ps <- survfit(cox_full, newdata = nd) tibble(month = ps$time, hiv_neg = ps$surv[, 1], hiv_pos = ps$surv[, 2]) |> pivot_longer(-month, names_to = "profile", values_to = "survival") |> ggplot(aes(month, survival, colour = profile)) + geom_step(linewidth = 1) + labs(x = "Months", y = "Predicted survival", colour = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s4_cox_regression_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: A **40-year-old man on DOT without MDR-TB or diabetes**, HIV-negative vs positive: the model gives the **expected curve** for any covariate pattern. ## HR is not a risk ratio ::: {.incremental} - An HR of 2 means the **rate** of dying is twice as high **at each moment**, not that the **cumulative risk** is doubled - With **rare** events they are close; with common events they differ - Report the HR **and** survival (or risk) at fixed times when possible ::: ## Reporting a Cox model ::: {.good} - **Events and patients** in each group; **median follow-up** - **Crude and adjusted HRs with 95% CI** (state the covariates and why) - The **reference** category and the **unit** of each continuous variable - The result of the **proportional-hazards check** (Session 5) ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 4 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `survival-workshop/labs/lab4_cox.R` - `coxph()` · `exp(coef())` · `confint()` - multivariable model, `tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE)` - rescale age · events per coefficient · predicted survival ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op8h3n.yhxmmg" data-show="QXQgYW55IHRpbWUsIHRoZSBoYXphcmQgb2YgZGVhdGggaXMgYWJvdXQgdHdpY2UgYXMgaGln aCB3aXRoIEhJVg==" data-explain="QSBoYXphcmQgcmF0aW8gY29tcGFyZXMgaW5zdGFudGFuZW91cyBldmVudCByYXRlcyBhdCBh bnkgdGltZS4gSXQgaXMgbm90IGEgcmF0aW8gb2YgY3VtdWxhdGl2ZSByaXNrcyBvciBvZiBz dXJ2aXZhbCB0aW1lcy4="} A Cox model gives HR = 2.0 (95% CI 1.2 to 3.3) for HIV-positive vs negative patients. Which interpretation is correct? - HIV-positive patients are twice as likely to die during the study - HIV-positive patients survive twice as long as negative patients - At any time, the hazard of death is about twice as high with HIV - Two per cent more HIV-positive patients die in every single month ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op8ucb.yhy13s" data-show="QWJvdXQgMS4yMiwgYmVjYXVzZSAxLjAyIG11bHRpcGxpZWQgYnkgaXRzZWxmIDEwIHRpbWVz " data-explain="SGF6YXJkIHJhdGlvcyBtdWx0aXBseTogMS4wMl4xMCDiiYggMS4yMi4gVGhlIHVuaXQgb2Yg YSBjb250aW51b3VzIHZhcmlhYmxlIG1hdHRlcnMsIHNvIHJlc2NhbGUgdG8gYSBtZWFuaW5n ZnVsIHN0ZXAu"} Age has HR = 1.02 per year. What is the approximate HR per 10 years? - About 1.20, because 0.02 is added 10 times - About 1.22, because 1.02 multiplied by itself 10 times - About 2.0, because 10 years doubles the hazard - About 1.02, since the hazard ratio does not depend on the unit ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op97l1.yhyfl6" data-show="SW5mb3JtYXRpb24gY29tZXMgZnJvbSBldmVudHM7IGNlbnNvcmVkIHBhdGllbnRzIGFkZCBh dC1yaXNrIHRpbWU=" data-explain="RXN0aW1hdGluZyBjb2VmZmljaWVudHMgcmVsaWVzIG9uIGNvbXBhcmluZyB3aG8gaGFzIHRo ZSBldmVudCB3aXRoIHdobyBpcyBhdCByaXNrLiBGZXcgZXZlbnRzIG1lYW4gdW5zdGFibGUg ZXN0aW1hdGVzLCB3aGF0ZXZlciB0aGUgbnVtYmVyIG9mIHBhdGllbnRzLg=="} Why is the number of events, not the number of patients, the key constraint on a Cox model? - Each patient appears just one time in the data set used to fit it - Cox models can only use the patients who died during follow-up - Information comes from events; censored patients add at-risk time - Censored patients are removed before the model is fitted to the rest ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op9ktr.yhyu2k" data-show="V2l0aCBvdGhlciB2YXJpYWJsZXMgZml4ZWQsIGhhemFyZCBvZiBkZWF0aCBpcyBhYm91dCA0 MyUgbG93ZXI=" data-explain="QW4gSFIgYmVsb3cgMSBpcyBhIGxvd2VyIGhhemFyZDogMSDiiJIgMC41NyA9IDQzJSBsb3dl ciwgYWRqdXN0ZWQgZm9yIHRoZSBvdGhlciB2YXJpYWJsZXMgaW4gdGhlIG1vZGVsLCByZWxh dGl2ZSB0byB0aGUgcmVmZXJlbmNlIGdyb3VwLg=="} In a Cox model the HR for treatment (DOT vs self-administered) is 0.57. What does this say? - DOT patients have a 57% probability of dying during follow-up - DOT patients live 43% longer than self-administered patients do - The hazard is 0.57 times lower with self-administered treatment - With other variables fixed, hazard of death is about 43% lower ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op9y2d.yhz8ju" data-show="VGhlIGhhemFyZCBmb3IgYSBwYXRpZW50IHdpdGggYWxsIGNvdmFyaWF0ZXMgYXQgcmVmZXJl bmNlIHZhbHVlcw==" data-explain="VGhlIENveCBtb2RlbCBsZWF2ZXMgdGhlIHNoYXBlIG9mIGgwKHQpIGZyZWUsIGVzdGltYXRp bmcgb25seSB0aGUgaGF6YXJkIHJhdGlvcy4gVGhhdCBpcyB3aHkgaXQgaXMgY2FsbGVkIHNl bWktcGFyYW1ldHJpYy4="} What is the baseline hazard h0(t) in the Cox model? - The hazard for a patient with all covariates at reference values - The proportion of patients who died during the follow-up period - The hazard ratio of the first predictor entered into the model - A constant rate that must be estimated before the model is fitted ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **HR = exp(β)**: the multiplicative change in the hazard, at any time - **Adjusted HRs** from a multivariable model; report CI and reference groups - **Rescale** continuous variables; check **events per coefficient** - HR is a **rate ratio**, not a risk ratio; the model can predict **survival curves** ::: **Next:** Session 5: assumptions and reporting

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
